68295-dulcie-carlyon-a-novel-volume-3-of.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. His present charger was not so steady as the old Cape nag, Tattoo, and Florian's hands, in the intensity of his excitement, trembled too much for his aim to be true; so the fugitives rode on and on, without firing a shot in return, thus showing that their ammunition had been expended, and they had nothing to hope for or trust to but a successful escape.

arxiv-2102-09947.title: Singular quasilinear convective elliptic systems in ℝ N \mathbb{R}^{N}
arxiv-2102-09947.creator: Umberto Guarnotta, Salvatore Angelo Marano
arxiv-2102-09947.description: Abstract The existence of a positive entire weak solution to a singular quasi-linear elliptic system with convection terms is established, chiefly through perturbation techniques, fixed point arguments, and a priori estimates. Some regularity results are then employed to show that the obtained solution is actually strong. Keywords: quasilinear elliptic system, gradient dependence, singular term, entire solution, strong solution.

arxiv-2208-10711.title: A Constrained Deformable Convolutional Network for Efficient Single Image Dynamic Scene Blind Deblurring with Spatially-Variant Motion Blur Kernels Estimation
arxiv-2208-10711.creator: Shu Tang, Yang Wu, Hongxing Qin, Xianzhong Xie, Shuli Yang, Jing Wang
arxiv-2208-10711.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Shu Tang, Yang Wu, Hongxing Qin, Xianzhong Xie, Shuli Yang, Jing Wang. Most existing deep-learning-based single image dynamic scene blind deblurring (SIDSBD) methods usually design deep networks to directly remove the spatially-variant motion blurs from one inputted motion blurred image, without blur kernels estimation. Recently, a reblurring training strategy has been proved that it can significantly boost the deblurring performance of deep-learning-based video blind deblurring (DLVBD) methods for the motion blurred video.

arxiv-2302-00959.title: Tilings of damaged hexagons
arxiv-2302-00959.creator: Markus Fulmek
arxiv-2302-00959.description: Abstract 1. Introduction In a recent paper [ 3 ] , Byun presented nice formulas for the enumeration of lozenge tilings of certain hexagonal regions with “intrusions”. This paper attempts to generalise some of Byun’s investigations. It is organised as follows: • In section 2 , we present the background needed for the considerations in this paper.

arxiv-2309-07063.title: Real-time quantum dynamics of thermal states with neural thermofields
arxiv-2309-07063.creator: Jannes Nys, Zakari Denis, Giuseppe Carleo
arxiv-2309-07063.description: Abstract Solving the time-dependent quantum many-body Schrödinger equation is a challenging task, especially for states at a finite temperature, where the environment affects the dynamics. Most existing approximating methods are designed to represent static thermal density matrices, 1D systems, and/or zero-temperature states.

arxiv-2411-00989.title: Automated Global Analysis of Experimental Dynamics through Low-Dimensional Linear Embeddings
arxiv-2411-00989.creator: Samuel A. Moore 1, Brian P. Mann 1, Boyuan Chen 1,2,3
arxiv-2411-00989.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Samuel A. Moore 1, Brian P. Mann 1, Boyuan Chen 1,2,3. Dynamical systems theory has long provided a foundation for understanding evolving phenomena across scientific domains. Yet, the application of this theory to complex real-world systems remains challenging due to issues in mathematical modeling, nonlinearity, and high dimensionality. In this work, we introduce a data-driven computational framework to derive low-dimensional linear models for nonlinear dynamical systems directly from raw experimental data.

arxiv-2510-16520.title: The deep-MOND limit – a study in Primary vs secondary predictions Bases on a talk presented at the MOND workshop, Leiden, September 2025.
arxiv-2510-16520.creator: Mordehai Milgrom
arxiv-2510-16520.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mordehai Milgrom. In default of a fundamental MOND theory – a FUNDAMOND – I advocate that, alongside searching for one, we should try to identify predictions that follow from wide classes of MOND theories, if not necessarily from all. In particular, predictions that follow from only the basic tenets of MOND – “primary predictions” – are shared by all MOND theories, and are especially valuable.

arxiv-2510-25434.title: A Critical Study of Automatic Evaluation in Sign Language Translation
arxiv-2510-25434.description: Abstract Automatic evaluation metrics are crucial for advancing sign language translation (SLT). Current SLT evaluation metrics, such as BLEU and ROUGE, are only text-based, and it remains unclear to what extent text-based metrics can reliably capture the quality of SLT outputs.

arxiv-2511-04571.title: Pseudo-dualizing complexes of torsion modules and semi-infinite MGM duality
arxiv-2511-04571.creator: Leonid Positselski
arxiv-2511-04571.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Leonid Positselski. This paper is an MGM version of [ 39 , 41 ] and a follow-up to [ 36 , Section 5] . In the setting of a commutative ring S S with a weakly proregular finitely generated ideal J ⊂ S J\subset S , we consider the maximal, abstract, and minimal corresponding classes of J J -torsion S S -modules and J J -contramodule S S -modules with respect to a given pseudo-dualizing complex of J J -torsion S S -modules L

arxiv-2512-05269.title: Eventually constant maps for two sets and nilpotent pairs
arxiv-2512-05269.creator: Weixi Chen, Mee Seong Im, Catherine Lillja, Nicolas Rugo
arxiv-2512-05269.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Weixi Chen, Mee Seong Im, Catherine Lillja, Nicolas Rugo. We give a bijective correspondence between the number of nilpotent matrices over a Boolean semiring and the number of directed acyclic graphs on ordered vertices. We then enumerate pairs of maps between two finite sets whose composites are eventually constant by forming a bijection that relates a pair of such maps with a spanning tree in a complete bipartite graph, and an edge of said tree. This generalizes the main principle of A.

pmc-11386358.title: Optimization of cassava (Manihot esculenta Crantz) grafting technique to enhance its adoption in cassava cultivation
pmc-11386358.creator: Frank Opoku-Agyemang, Jacqueline Naalamle Amissah, Stella Owusu-Nketia, Peter Amoako Ofori, Michitaka Notaguchi
pmc-11386358.description: Grafting techniques have been successfully adopted to improve resistance to biotic and abiotic stresses, increase yields, fruit quality and study systemic signaling in plants. This technique has not been fully explored in cassava and there is currently no standardized grafting method for this species published especially in Africa.

pmc-11401408.title: Whole-genome resequencing reveals melanin deposition candidate genes of Luning chicken
pmc-11401408.creator: Chuwen Chen, Jie Li, Zhiyi Li, Yi Nong, Jiayan Wang, Zi Wang, Zhixiong Li
pmc-11401408.description: BackgroundMelanin in the black-bone chicken’s body is considered the material basis for its medicinal effects and is an economically important trait. Therefore, improving the melanin content is a crucial focus in the breeding process of black-bone chickens. Luning chickens are black-bone chickens, with black beaks, skin, and meat.

pmc-12539087.title: Surgical intervention of mitral valve aneurysm: a case report
pmc-12539087.creator: Kazuki Mori, Satoshi Takebayashi, Masato Morita, Masazumi Kume, Yuichi Nakazono
pmc-12539087.description: BackgroundMitral valve aneurysm is a rare structural abnormality characterized by a saccular protrusion of the mitral valve leaflet. The diagnosis of a mitral valve aneurysm can be challenging, especially when echocardiography fails to show a clear saccular appearance.Case presentationA 66-year-old male patient exhibited no symptoms but demonstrated echocardiographic findings indicative of a suspected cardiac tumor on the anterior mitral leaflet.

pmc-12598819.title: A survey on the current status of Korean Medicine practices for asthma among Korean Medicine doctors
pmc-12598819.creator: Soo-Dam Kim, Sungha Kim, Hee-Jae Jung, Kwan-Il Kim, Yee Ran Lyu, Beom-Joon Lee
pmc-12598819.description: BackgroundAsthma is a chronic respiratory disease affecting millions of people worldwide, with a growing prevalence in South Korea. Korean medicine (KM), which includes herbal medicine, acupuncture, moxibustion, cupping, and other holistic therapies, is widely used for asthma treatment in South Korea. However, data on the clinical practices of Korean medicine doctors (KMDs) are limited.

pmc-12720443.title: Antisense transcription can induce expression memory via stable promoter repression
pmc-12720443.creator: Verena Mutzel, Till Schwämmle, Svearike Oeverdieck, Lucija Librenjak, Benedikt Boesen, Melissa Bothe, Rutger A. F. Gjaltema, Ilona Dunkel, Gemma Noviello, Edda G. Schulz
pmc-12720443.description: BackgroundThe capacity of cells to retain a memory of previous signals enables acquisition of unique fates and adaptation to their environment. The underlying gene expression memory can arise from mutual repression of two genes, forming a toggle switch. Mutual repression can occur at antisense loci, where convergent genes repress each other in cis.

pmc-12996185.title: Established and emerging non-cellular therapies in inherited bone marrow failure syndromes
pmc-12996185.creator: Szymon Janczar, Bartosz Urbański, Marek Ussowicz, Wojciech Mlynarski
pmc-12996185.description: Inherited bone marrow failure syndromes (IBMFs) are a molecularly heterogeneous group of genetically-determined syndromes with a wide spectrum of clinical abnormalities and risk of hematopoietic neoplasia and reduced life expectancy. The prevalence is not well established but is growing due to the advent of genetic diagnostics.

pmc-13032318.title: Animal models for critical-sized long-bone defects and long-bone non-union: a scoping review
pmc-13032318.creator: Nader Maai, Arthur Meuris, FRI Research Group Basel, Esther Wehrle, Willem-Jan Metsemakers, Claudia Siverino, Mario Morgenstern
pmc-13032318.description: BackgroundCritical-sized long-bone defects and non-unions are among the most challenging complications in fracture care, as they lack the capacity for spontaneous healing and often lead to prolonged disability and repeated surgical intervention. Their complex aetiology involves mechanical, biological, and systemic factors that make consistent clinical management difficult.

pmc-13272015.title: Safety profile of ipilimumab in elderly patients: a disproportionate analysis based on the FDA Adverse Event Reporting System database
pmc-13272015.creator: Yang Yang, Fang Wang, Weijia Tong, Xinglan Lu, Feng Zhao, Shencun Fang, Shiqiao Wang
pmc-13272015.description: BackgroundIpilimumab is the first cytotoxic T lymphocyte protein-4 (CTLA-4) inhibitor approved in the United States. However, there is insufficient data on the safety of this drug in elderly patients. This study aimed to identify adverse events (AEs) associated with ipilimumab in elderly patients through the Adverse Event Reporting System (FAERS) database.

pmc-13372067.title: Unusual Coexistence of Takayasu Arteritis, Diffuse Coronary Aneurysms, and a Large Left Atrial Myxoma in an Elderly Male: A Case Report and Literature Review
pmc-13372067.creator: Aoumar G Chamma, Wendy Saliba, Linda Chamma

pmc-13449855.title: Effectiveness of different modes of digital health interventions for sarcopenia in older adults: a systematic review and network meta-analysis
pmc-13449855.creator: Jiayi Yao, Haozhe Wang, Junhao He, Wenjia Chen
pmc-13449855.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background and objectiveSarcopenia-related disability in older adults has emerged as a serious public health challenge; however, the relative efficacy of digital health interventions delivered through different technological pathways in this population remains unclear.

pmc-13590278.title: Host Call Frequency Drives Attractiveness to an Eavesdropping Micropredator
pmc-13590278.creator: Timothy P Cutajar, Alistair G B Poore, Jodi J L Rowley
pmc-13590278.description: Acoustic sexual signals are vulnerable to interception by eavesdropping predators, micropredators and parasitoids. Signal traits can impact attractiveness to eavesdroppers and potential mates alike. Thus, signals are influenced by interacting selection pressures and drive predator/prey interactions and their consequences (e.g., disease dynamics where eavesdroppers are vectors).
